name: Paper Folding
shortcutSummary: Track each fold carefully: which part overlaps which. When holes are punched, unfold in reverse order. Each fold doubles the number of holes symmetrically.
conceptExplanation:
Paper Folding questions show a sequence: a paper is folded in specific directions, then a hole/cut is made. You must determine how the paper looks when fully unfolded.

Key concept: Each fold creates symmetry. When you unfold, holes appear symmetrically about the fold line.

subtopics.name: Paper Folding — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation:
Paper Folding questions show a sequence: a paper is folded in specific directions, then a hole/cut is made. You must determine how the paper looks when fully unfolded.

Key concept: Each fold creates symmetry. When you unfold, holes appear symmetrically about the fold line.
shortcuts: Reverse Unfold: Unfold in the exact reverse order of folding.
Symmetry About Fold Line: Holes appear as mirror images about each fold line.
Count Multiplication: Each fold doubles the holes. Two folds = 4 holes from one punch.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A transparent square sheet has a design:
Left half: a circle with a vertical diameter.
Right half: a circle with a horizontal diameter.
Find out how the pattern will appear when the transparent sheet is folded along the central dotted line (left half is folded over the right half along the vertical dotted line).
options: a single circle with both horizontal and vertical diameters (cross inside circle)
A circle with only the vertical diameter remaining
A circle with two parallel vertical chords
A circle divided into four quadrants with one quadrant shaded
practiceQuestions.hint: Folding along a vertical axis creates a lateral mirror reflection of the folded half onto the stationary half.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Folding the left half over the right half superimposes the vertical diameter onto the right circle, intersecting the horizontal diameter into a full cross (+).
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Identify which half is stationary and which half moves.
Step 2: Reflect the moving design across the fold line as a mirror image.
Step 3: Superimpose the reflected design onto the stationary design to obtain: a single circle with both horizontal and vertical diameters (cross inside circle).

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A transparent square sheet has a design:
Left half: an upward pointing equilateral triangle.
Right half: a downward pointing equilateral triangle.
Find out how the pattern will appear when the transparent sheet is folded along the central dotted line (left side is folded over the right side along the central vertical axis).
options: Two disjoint triangles touching only at their apex
a six-pointed star (hexagram) formed by the two superimposed triangles
A single upward-pointing triangle with a horizontal base line
A diamond (rhombus) formed by inverted triangular bases
practiceQuestions.hint: Folding along a vertical axis creates a lateral mirror reflection of the folded half onto the stationary half.
practiceQuestions.explanation: When the upward triangle on the left folds onto the downward triangle on the right, their outlines intersect to create a symmetrical six-pointed star.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Identify which half is stationary and which half moves.
Step 2: Reflect the moving design across the fold line as a mirror image.
Step 3: Superimpose the reflected design onto the stationary design to obtain: a six-pointed star (hexagram) formed by the two superimposed triangles.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
A transparent square sheet has a design:
Left half: a solid dark square in the top-left corner.
Right half: an open circle in the top-right corner.
Find out how the pattern will appear when the transparent sheet is folded along the central dotted line (the transparent sheet is folded from left to right along the vertical dotted midline).
options: A square sheet half with both square and circle superimposed in top-left
A square sheet half with only the square remaining visible
a solid dark square completely enclosing the open circle in the top-right quadrant
A square sheet half containing the dark square at top-left and dark circle at top-right
practiceQuestions.hint: Folding along a vertical axis creates a lateral mirror reflection of the folded half onto the stationary half.
practiceQuestions.explanation: The solid square in the top-left flips laterally across the vertical midline into the top-right quadrant, superimposing over the circle.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Identify which half is stationary and which half moves.
Step 2: Reflect the moving design across the fold line as a mirror image.
Step 3: Superimpose the reflected design onto the stationary design to obtain: a solid dark square completely enclosing the open circle in the top-right quadrant.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
